universities.name: University of Bonn
universities.summary: The University of Bonn is a public research university in Bonn, founded in 1818. Its English-taught M.Sc. Computer Science is a four-semester, 120-ECTS programme with specializations in Algorithmics, Graphics/Vision/Audio, Information and Communication Management, and Intelligent Systems.
universities.campusLifestyle: Bonn’s main university sites include the historic main building and the Poppelsdorf campus. The Computer Science Institute is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences; the degree is organized as a research-oriented single-subject master’s programme rather than a taught conversion course.
universities.cityProfile: Bonn is a former federal capital on the Rhine and a UN location. The university’s current international-student guidance estimates living costs at roughly EUR 1,000 a month; its detailed planning table lists average rent of EUR 410, food EUR 198, health care EUR 100 and communication EUR 31. These are planning figures, not a fixed student budget.
universities.practicalExposure: The M.Sc. programme is organized around research areas rather than a mandatory employer-placement promise. Bonn publishes four specializations—Algorithmics, Graphics/Vision/Audio, Information and Communication Management, and Intelligent Systems—and identifies a 12-ECTS research thesis among the specific prior-learning requirements, signalling that the programme expects applicants to arrive with research-method preparation.
universities.hostelOverview: Student housing is handled by Studierendenwerk Bonn, which accepts applications for dormitory places. The university’s 2025–26 exchange fact sheet gives planning ranges of EUR 300–560 a month for dormitory housing and EUR 300–650 for private accommodation; availability and the actual contract cost vary by residence and intake.
universities.dietarySupport: Bonn’s published cost table budgets EUR 198 a month for food. The university does not present this as a compulsory meal-plan charge; it is a planning figure within a wider student-living estimate, alongside rent, health insurance, learning materials and personal expenses.
universities.safetyOverview: The university’s international guidance focuses on practical arrival and residence support rather than publishing campus-crime statistics. Students who need a German study visa must show sufficient funding; Bonn notes the federal minimum cited for this purpose is EUR 992 per month or EUR 11,904 per year from October 2024.
universities.studentSupport: The International Office provides application and arrival information, while Studierendenwerk Bonn manages student-housing applications. Bonn’s Study Buddy Program matches newly arrived international students with local students, and Welcome Days are held before semesters for international arrivals.
whyChoose: English-taught M.Sc. Computer Science with a defined four-semester, 120-ECTS structure.
Four published research specializations: Algorithmics, Graphics/Vision/Audio, Information and Communication Management, and Intelligent Systems.
No tuition for the regular public-university programme; the current Winter Semester 2026/27 social contribution is published as EUR 363.07.
System accreditation granted in March 2026 by the German Accreditation Council framework.
thingsToConsider: Admission is locally restricted and requires a relevant first degree plus specified prior credits; a general computing degree title alone may not satisfy the module requirements.
English C1 is required for the programme, despite studying in Germany where many other degree programmes use German.
The social contribution is not tuition and changes by semester; living costs remain the larger recurring budget item.
A non-EU applicant may need visa funding evidence in addition to the programme’s academic admission requirements.
bestFitFor: Computer Science graduates with documented mathematics, algorithms/formal-languages, programming/software-engineering and research-thesis credits.
Applicants seeking an English research master’s with winter or summer entry rather than a conversion programme.
Students able to plan for Bonn living costs and the German residence-permit funding requirement.

faq.question: Is the Bonn M.Sc. Computer Science taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The University of Bonn degree listing identifies English as the language of instruction and sets English proficiency at CEFR C1 for admission.

faq.question: How long is the programme?
faq.answer: The standard full-time period is four semesters and the Institute of Computer Science lists 120 ECTS. A part-time route is listed as six semesters.

faq.question: Does Bonn charge tuition for this programme?
faq.answer: The University of Bonn states that regular public-university study has no tuition. Students pay a changing social contribution each semester; Winter Semester 2026/27 is listed at EUR 363.07.

faq.question: What prior study is required?
faq.answer: Applicants need a relevant university degree, English C1 and specified prior modules in mathematics, algorithm theory/complexity/formal languages, programming/software engineering/information systems, plus a research thesis.

faq.question: When can students start?
faq.answer: The degree listing shows winter-semester and summer-semester starts. The programme’s admission procedure is locally restricted, so the applicable deadline and selection route should be built into the application plan.

faq.question: What does Bonn estimate for living costs?
faq.answer: Its international-student guidance gives a rough EUR 1,000 monthly estimate. The detailed table identifies rent, food, health care and communication as separate planning components.

universities.name: TU Dresden
universities.summary: TU Dresden is a public technical university in Dresden, founded in 1828. Its English-language M.Sc. Computer Science began with the Winter Semester 2025/26 curriculum, runs over four semesters, and offers an Open Track or a Distributed Systems Engineering track.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Faculty of Computer Science is based on TU Dresden’s main campus. The degree’s third semester is deliberately structured so students can use it for a temporary stay at another university; this is an option, not an included exchange entitlement.
universities.cityProfile: TU Dresden’s international factsheet lists EUR 230–500 a month as a student-accommodation planning range. For the 2026 winter semester, the on-campus semester fee is EUR 361, including EUR 112.73 for Studentenwerk and EUR 248.27 for the student body and transport/bike services.
universities.practicalExposure: The research-oriented programme includes a research project in the third semester and a fourth-semester master’s thesis and colloquium. Its two tracks organize advanced work differently: Open Track draws from eight subject areas, while Distributed Systems Engineering is a dedicated track; neither structure promises a job placement.
universities.hostelOverview: TU Dresden directs students to Studentenwerk Dresden for housing. Its international factsheet gives an indicative EUR 230–500 monthly accommodation range and notes kitchen facilities in student residences; the actual room, wait time and contract are determined by the housing provider.
universities.dietarySupport: The university’s current semester contribution funds student-services and student-body provision, but it is not a meal plan. TU Dresden publishes no single compulsory food budget for this master’s programme, so food should be planned separately from the EUR 361 semester fee.
universities.safetyOverview: TU Dresden’s international FAQ gives practical enrollment guidance, including health-insurance formalities and any missing documents named in an admission letter. It does not publish campus-specific safety statistics, so this page does not make a comparative safety claim.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants with a foreign higher-education entrance qualification are directed through TU Dresden’s online application route, commonly to uni-assist; all applicants also submit a separate aptitude-assessment application. ServiceCenterStudies is the first contact point for Admissions and International Office matters.
whyChoose: English-language M.Sc. Computer Science with C1-level admission standard and a four-semester structure.
Two documented curriculum choices: Open Track and Distributed Systems Engineering.
A third-semester research project and fourth-semester thesis/colloquium structure.
Regular on-campus study has a published semester contribution rather than a general tuition charge.
thingsToConsider: Admission is an aptitude-assessment process; the decision is accept or reject and conditions cannot be imposed to repair missing subject requirements.
Applicants need a Computer Science first degree and 90 ECTS across three defined subject groups.
International winter applications with an overseas entrance qualification are accepted only from April 1 to May 31; the summer window is October 1 to November 30.
The semester fee changes each term and additional tuition can apply for specific situations such as long-term study.
bestFitFor: Computer Science graduates whose transcript can document the published 35/35/20 ECTS subject distribution.
Applicants with C1 English evidence who can manage a two-part application and aptitude assessment.
Students seeking a research-oriented master’s with a defined distributed-systems option.

faq.question: Is TU Dresden M.Sc. Computer Science taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes. TU Dresden identifies the programme as English-language and requires C1 CEFR English for admission.

faq.question: How long is the programme?
faq.answer: The programme is spread across four semesters. The third semester contains the research project and is structured to allow a temporary stay at another university; the fourth is reserved for the thesis and colloquium.

faq.question: What undergraduate background is required?
faq.answer: Applicants need a first professionally qualifying Computer Science degree and 90 ECTS of non-overlapping prior study across specified systems, mathematics/theory/AI, and programming/software-engineering groups.

faq.question: Is the GRE required?
faq.answer: TU Dresden strongly recommends GRE General Test results for international applicants with a bachelor’s degree from outside the EU or EEA. Its admission page describes this as a recommendation, not a blanket mandatory condition.

faq.question: What are the international application dates?
faq.answer: For foreign higher-education entrance qualifications, the programme lists April 1–May 31 for winter entry and October 1–November 30 for the following summer entry.

faq.question: What does it cost to enroll?
faq.answer: The regular 2026 winter-semester fee for on-campus students is EUR 361. TU Dresden explains that tuition may additionally apply in defined cases such as long-term study or certain special courses.

universities.name: University of Naples Federico II
universities.summary: The University of Naples Federico II is a public university in Naples, founded in 1224. Its School of Medicine offers a six-year, 360-ECTS English course in Medicine and Surgery for EU and non-EU high-school graduates, with integrated basic and clinical teaching and placements.
universities.campusLifestyle: The English Medicine and Surgery programme is run through Federico II’s School of Medicine and Federico II Hospital. Its official brochure identifies the student office at Via Sergio Pansini 5 and the International Students’ office at Corso Umberto I 40, separating academic administration from international administrative support.
universities.cityProfile: Naples is a large southern Italian city, and the university’s public medicine brochure does not set a single living-cost figure. Tuition is described as based on certified family income (ISEEU) and excludes food and accommodation, so a complete budget requires a current individual fee assessment plus housing and daily-living planning.
universities.practicalExposure: The official English Medicine and Surgery brochure describes a six-year, 360-ECTS curriculum that integrates basic and clinical courses. It lists laboratory teaching, workshops, small-group tutorials, seminars and clinical placements in primary and secondary care, with internship and an experimental thesis as integral parts of the programme.
universities.hostelOverview: Federico II directs students to ADISU Federico II for housing information. The public course brochure does not publish a guaranteed room, a residence rate or a universal private-rental range, so accommodation should be secured as a separate step after the programme and regional-support route are understood.
universities.dietarySupport: The medicine brochure expressly excludes food and accommodation from tuition. Federico II does not publish an English Medicine-specific meal-plan price in that brochure, so the cost plan should separate tuition assessment, housing, food, transport, insurance and administrative charges.
universities.safetyOverview: The programme’s public materials provide student-office, medical-school and international-office contact routes but do not publish campus-specific safety statistics. This page therefore describes the available administrative support without asserting a comparative safety outcome.
universities.studentSupport: International students are supported through Federico II’s International Students’ office and the university’s online administrative platform, Segrepass. The 2026/27 enrollment guidance states that restricted-access programmes follow the methods and deadlines set in their published calls, rather than the open-admission enrollment route.

Integrated basic and clinical teaching with laboratory sessions, workshops, primary- and secondary-care placements, internship and thesis.
The programme is explicitly described for EU and non-EU resident and non-resident high-school graduates.

faq.question: Is Medicine and Surgery at Federico II taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The School of Medicine brochure identifies an English Course in Medicine and Surgery. It is a six-year programme; the course also includes institutional English-language study at B1 and B2 levels for students who do not hold an accepted certificate.

faq.question: How long is the medicine programme?
faq.answer: The published programme length is six years, 12 semesters and 360 ECTS. Internship and an experimental thesis are integral components.

faq.question: Can non-EU applicants apply?
faq.answer: The programme brochure states that it is intended for EU and non-EU resident and non-resident high-school graduates. The applicant must still satisfy the current international pre-enrolment and restricted-access procedures.

faq.question: Is admission open to everyone who meets the academic requirements?
faq.answer: No. Medicine and Surgery in English is restricted access. Federico II states that candidates register for the admission test and admission depends on test score and position in the candidate list.

faq.question: Does Federico II publish one medicine tuition price?
faq.answer: The public English Medicine brochure says tuition is based on certified family income (ISEEU) and does not include food or accommodation. A current individual fee assessment is needed for a usable total-cost plan.

faq.question: What learning and clinical experience is documented?
faq.answer: The brochure lists tutorials, seminars, laboratory teaching, workshops and clinical placements in primary and secondary care. It also describes internship and an experimental thesis as integral to the course.
